Admittedly the respondent No.1 and 2 are the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No1 insurance company has taken up defence that, the driver of the offending lorry did not possess the valid driving license to driver the tanker lorry which is hazardous one.

In the charge sheet and other document including the insurance policy it is not mentioned that offending vehicle is a fuel tanker lorry, except mentioning  SCCH4 21 MVC No.5481 and  5482/2019 as tanker lorry.
Mere a word 'tanker lorry' does not mean that, hazardous vehicle, unless the respondent prove that, the offending lorry is a fuel container lorry or any other hazardous vehicle.
Hence, the contention of respondent No.1 is not acceptable under law.
In terms of the insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.1 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation behalf of the respondent No.2 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

The petitions filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner in MVC No.5481/2019 is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,34,036/ (Rupees Six Lakhs Thirty Four Thousand and Thirty Six Only) along with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till realization of the amount.

The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
